findings.title: Date override timezone conversion uses the wrong sign for the organizer UTC offset
findings.body: In checkIfIsAvailable, the organizer's UTC offset is applied with a negated sign: `const utcOffset = organizerTimeZone ? dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1 : 0;` and then `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes")`. Date overrides are stored as UTC instants representing local wall-clock times in the organizer's timezone (e.g. a 14:00 IST override is stored as 08:30 UTC). To compare the override's wall-clock date against the slot's UTC date, the offset must be ADDED (converting the stored UTC instant back to organizer-local wall-clock), not subtracted. Negating it shifts the override by twice the offset (e.g. 11 hours for IST instead of 5:30), so the 'YYYY MM DD' comparison at line 110-112 matches the wrong day for any organizer whose offset is non-zero. Consequence: for round-robin events with fixed hosts, slots on the override day are incorrectly rejected (or slots on adjacent days incorrectly accepted), meaning fixed-host date overrides are not reliably honored — the exact bug this PR claims to fix. The same negated-offset pattern also appears in the working-hours fallback check below it, compounding the error.

findings.title: Equality comparison of Dayjs objects with === never matches, making all-day (unavailable) overrides ineffective
findings.body: Line 114 uses `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` to detect an all-day-unavailable override (start == end). Dayjs objects are compared by reference with ===, so this is always false even when the two instants are identical. As a result, an override that marks a whole day as unavailable (start equals end, the standard representation for a blocked day) falls through to the subsequent range checks, which compare slotStartTime/slotEndTime against a zero-length interval and never return true — so the override is treated as if it doesn't exist and the day's normal working hours are used. Consequence: fixed hosts' all-day unavailability overrides are ignored for round-robin events, allowing bookings on days the fixed host explicitly blocked.

findings.title: Extra closing parenthesis makes the slotStartTime.isAfter check a no-op
findings.body: Line 123 reads `if (slotStartTime.isAfter(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes"))) {` — there is an unbalanced extra `)` before the opening brace. The condition `slotStartTime.isAfter(...)` is evaluated and its boolean result is discarded (it becomes the expression statement of the if with an empty body effect), and `return true` executes unconditionally whenever the date comparison on line 110 matched. This means any slot on the override's day is treated as 'outside the override' and rejected, regardless of whether it actually falls after the override end. Combined with the sign error above, the override window boundaries are computed incorrectly. Consequence: slots after the override end time on the override day are wrongly excluded (or, depending on the other branches, the whole day's logic misfires), producing incorrect availability for fixed hosts.

findings.title: Working-hours fallback check compares slot start to both startTime and endTime using the same value
findings.body: In the working-hours fallback inside checkIfIsAvailable (lines 139-147), `const start = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute(); const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` — `end` is assigned the slot START in minutes, not the slot end (start + eventLength). The check `if (start < workingHour.startTime || end > workingHour.endTime) return true;` therefore never detects a slot that starts inside working hours but extends past endTime. Consequence: for fixed hosts in round-robin events, slots that overrun the end of the working day are not rejected by this check, so the event can appear bookable at times the fixed host is not actually available (the busy-time check at the end may still catch some cases, but availability-window enforcement is broken).

findings.title: Selected-slot filtering returns false for users with no reserved slots, dropping all round-robin hosts
findings.body: In the selectedSlots filtering block (lines 565-590), for each slot userId the code builds `busy` from that user's reserved (non-seat) selectedSlots and then: `if (!busy?.length && eventType.seatsPerTimeSlot === null) { return false; }`. For a round-robin event (seatsPerTimeSlot === null) where a loose host has no reserved slot at that time, `busy` is empty and the userId is filtered OUT of the slot — even though the host is simply free. This inverts the intended semantics (a host with no reservation should remain available). Consequence: whenever any selected slot exists for the event (selectedSlots.length > 0), all round-robin hosts without a reservation are removed from every slot, which can empty the slot list entirely and make the event appear fully booked. This is a pre-existing logic error in this block that the PR's changes interact with, and it directly affects round-robin availability.

findings.title: Override timezone conversion uses the override's own timeZone field, which is not populated for user-level overrides
findings.body: In getSlots, the override offset is computed as `const organizerUtcOffset = dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone).utcOffset();`. The `timeZone` property on date overrides is only added in this PR to the flattened overrides in slots.ts (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts line 410-416) and to the TimeRange type; it comes from `availability.timeZone` (the user's timezone). However, getSlots is also called from client-side code and other paths where overrides may not carry `timeZone` (the type marks it optional). When `override.timeZone` is undefined, `dayjs(...).tz(undefined)` falls back to the runtime's local timezone, producing an offset based on the server/browser local zone rather than the organizer's zone. Consequence: the invitee-facing slot computation can shift override windows by the wrong amount for any caller that doesn't populate timeZone, reintroducing the timezone bug this PR fixes on those paths.

findings.title: Override start/end minutes computed in two separate dayjs chains can straddle a DST boundary inconsistently
findings.body: Lines 218-223 compute startTime and endTime via two independent expressions: `dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, "minute").hour() * 60 + dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, "minute").minute()` and the same for `override.end`. The offset is derived from `override.start` only (line 212-213). If the override window crosses a DST transition in the invitee timezone (or organizer timezone), the offset computed at `override.start` is applied to `override.end` as well, so the end time can be off by the DST delta (typically 60 minutes). Consequence: override windows spanning a DST change produce slots shifted by an hour at the end of the window on the booking page.

findings.title: New timezone test only verifies identical output, not that the override shifts with the invitee timezone
findings.body: The added test 'scheduleForEventOnADayWithDateOverrideDifferentTimezone' (lines 788-804) queries with timeZone Asia/Dhaka (+6:00) and asserts the exact same UTC slots as the IST query, with the comment 'it should return the same as this is the utc time'. Since getSchedule returns slots as UTC ISO strings, identical UTC output across invitee timezones is expected and does not exercise the fix: the PR's second fix is that the override window (defined in organizer local time) must be interpreted in the organizer's timezone and rendered correctly for any invitee timezone. A meaningful test would use an invitee timezone where the override day/window maps to a different UTC day (e.g. a negative-offset zone like America/New_York, where 14:00-18:00 IST is 03:30-07:30 UTC same day but the date-override day boundary shifts), and assert the slots land on the correct UTC day. As written, the test would pass even if the offset logic in packages/lib/slots.ts were wrong by up to several hours, so it provides no regression protection for the timezone fix.

findings.title: No test covers date overrides for fixed hosts in round-robin events, which is the PR's primary fix
findings.body: The PR description states the main fix is that 'date overrides of fixed hosts are taken into account for round-robin events', but the only new/changed test ('Check for Date overrides', line 742) uses a single-user event with `hosts: []` and no `schedulingType: "ROUND_ROBIN"`. The new checkIfIsAvailable date-override/working-hours logic (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts lines 102-151) is only exercised through the fixed-hosts filter path (line 483-499) for round-robin/team events with hosts; no test creates a ROUND_ROBIN event with a fixed host that has a date override and asserts that slots outside the override are removed. Given the sign error, no-op equality, and syntax-level issues in that new code (see other findings), the primary behavior the PR claims to fix is completely untested and would not be caught by CI.
